# camino-tempfile 1.4.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/camino-tempfile/latest/source/README.md

```
[![camino-tempfile on crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/camino-tempfile)](https://crates.io/crates/camino-tempfile)
[![Documentation (latest release)](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-latest%20version-brightgreen.svg)](https://docs.rs/camino-tempfile)
[![Documentation (main)](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-main-purple.svg)](https://camino-rs.github.io/camino-tempfile/rustdoc/camino_tempfile/)
[![License (Apache 2.0)](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache-green.svg)](LICENSE-APACHE)
[![License (MIT)](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE-MIT)
A secure, cross-platform, temporary file library for Rust with UTF-8 paths.
This crate is a wrapper around [`tempfile`](https://crates.io/crates/tempfile) that works with the `Utf8Path` and `Utf8PathBuf` types defined by [`camino`](https://crates.io/crates/camino). If your code mostly uses `camino`, it can be annoying to have to convert temporary paths to
`Utf8Path` over and over again. This crate manages that for you.
In addition to creating temporary files, this library also allows users to securely open multiple independent references to the same temporary file (useful for consumer/producer patterns and surprisingly difficult to implement securely).
This crate closely mirrors tempfile's interface. For extensions that provide quality-of-life improvements such as the ability to create files easily, see [`camino-tempfile-ext`](https://crates.io/crates/camino-tempfile-ext).
[Documentation](https://docs.rs/camino-tempfile)
Add this to your Cargo.toml:
```toml
[dependencies]
camino-tempfile = "1"
```
```rust
use std::fs::File;
use std::io::{Write, Read, Seek, SeekFrom};
fn main() {
}
```
camino-tempfile's MSRV is **Rust 1.74**. At any time, at least the last 6 months of Rust releases will be supported.
This project is available under the terms of either the [Apache 2.0 license](LICENSE-APACHE) or the [MIT
license](LICENSE-MIT).
Portions copied and adapted from [tempfile](https://github.com/Stebalien/tempfile) and used under the MIT and Apache 2.0 licenses. tempfile is copyright 2015 Steven Allen and the tempfile authors.
```

# camino 1.2.4 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/camino/1.2.4

# camino - UTF-8 paths

This repository contains the source code for `camino`, an extension of the `std::path` module that adds new
[ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/camino/*/camino/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html) and

[types.](https://docs.rs/camino/*/camino/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`## What is camino?

`camino`'s [ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/camino/*/camino/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html) and

[types are like the standard library's](https://docs.rs/camino/*/camino/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html)

`PathBuf`[types, except they are guaranteed to only contain UTF-8 encoded data. Therefore, they expose the ability to get their contents as strings, they implement](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/path/struct.Path.html)

`Path``Display`, etc.The `std::path` types are not guaranteed to be valid UTF-8. This is the right decision for the standard library,
since it must be as general as possible. However, on all platforms, non-Unicode paths are vanishingly uncommon for a
number of reasons:

- Unicode is now the dominant encoding for file names. There are still some legacy codebases that store paths in encodings like [Shift JIS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shift_JIS), but most have been converted to Unicode at this point.
- Unicode is the common subset of supported paths across Windows and Unix platforms. (On Windows, Rust stores paths
as [an extension to UTF-8](https://simonsapin.github.io/wtf-8/), and converts them to UTF-16 at Win32 API boundaries.)
- There are already many systems, such as Cargo, that only support UTF-8 paths. If your own tool interacts with any such system, you can assume that paths are valid UTF-8 without creating any additional burdens on consumers.
- The ["makefile problem"](https://www.mercurial-scm.org/wiki/EncodingStrategy#The_.22makefile_problem.22)asks: given a Makefile or other metadata file (such as`Cargo.toml`) that lists the names of other files, how should the names in the Makefile be matched with the ones on disk? This has*no general, cross-platform solution*in systems that support non-UTF-8 paths. However, restricting paths to UTF-8 eliminates this problem.

Therefore, many programs that want to manipulate paths *do* assume they contain UTF-8 data, and convert them to `str`s
as necessary. However, because this invariant is not encoded in the `Path` type, conversions such as
`path.to_str().unwrap()` need to be repeated again and again, creating a frustrating experience.

Instead, `camino` allows you to check that your paths are UTF-8 *once*, and then manipulate them
as valid UTF-8 from there on, avoiding repeated lossy and confusing conversions.

## Examples

The documentation for [ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/camino/*/camino/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html) and

[contains several examples.](https://docs.rs/camino/*/camino/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`For examples of how to use `camino` with other libraries like `serde` and `clap`, see the [ camino-examples](https://github.com/camino-rs/camino/tree/main/camino-examples) directory.

## API design

`camino` is a very thin wrapper around `std::path`. [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/camino/*/camino/struct.Utf8Path.html) and

[are drop-in replacements for](https://docs.rs/camino/*/camino/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html)

`Utf8PathBuf`[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/path/struct.Path.html)

`Path`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html)

`PathBuf`Most APIs are the same, but those at the boundary with `str` are different. Some examples:

- `Path::to_str() -> Option<&str>`has been renamed to- `Utf8Path::as_str() -> &str`.
- `Utf8Path`- `Display`, and- `Path::display()`has been removed.
- Iterating over a `Utf8Path``&str`, not`&OsStr`.

Every [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/camino/*/camino/struct.Utf8Path.html) is a valid

[, so](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/path/struct.Path.html)

`Path`[implements](https://docs.rs/camino/*/camino/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path``AsRef<Path>`. Any APIs that accept `impl AsRef<Path>`
will continue to work with [instances.](https://docs.rs/camino/*/camino/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`## Should you use camino?

`camino` trades off some utility for a great deal of simplicity. Whether `camino` is appropriate for a project or not
is ultimately a case-by-case decision. Here are some general guidelines that may help.

*You should consider using camino if...*

- **You're building portable, cross-platform software.**While both Unix and Windows platforms support different kinds of non-Unicode paths, Unicode is the common subset that's supported across them.
- **Your system has files that contain the names of other files.**If you don't use UTF-8 paths, you will run into the makefile problem described above, which has no general, cross-platform solution.
- **You're interacting with existing systems that already assume UTF-8 paths.**In that case you won't be adding any new burdens on downstream consumers.
- **You're building something brand new and are willing to ask your users to rename their paths if necessary.**Projects that don't have to worry about legacy compatibility have more flexibility in choosing what paths they support.

In general, using camino is the right choice for most projects.

*You should  NOT use camino, if...*

- **You're writing a core system utility.**If you're writing, say, an- `mv`or- `cat`replacement, you should- **not**use camino. Instead, use- `std::path::Path`
- **You have legacy compatibility constraints.**For example, Git supports non-UTF-8 paths. If your tool needs to handle arbitrary Git repositories, it should use its own path type that's a wrapper around- `Vec<u8>`.- `std::path::Path`- [on Unix](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/os/unix/ffi/index.html)but not on Windows.

- **There's some other reason you need to support non-UTF-8 paths.**Some tools like disk recovery utilities need to handle potentially corrupt filenames: only being able to handle UTF-8 paths would greatly diminish their utility.

## Optional features

By default, `camino` has **no dependencies** other than `std`. There are some optional features that enable
dependencies:

- `serde1`adds serde- `Serialize`- `Deserialize`- `Utf8PathBuf`- `Utf8Path`
- `proptest1`adds- [proptest](https://altsysrq.github.io/proptest-book/)- `Arbitrary`- `Utf8PathBuf`- `Box<Utf8Path>`.

## Rust version support

The minimum supported Rust version (MSRV) for `camino` with default features is **1.61**. This project is tested in CI
against the latest stable version of Rust and the MSRV.

- *Stable APIs*added in later Rust versions are supported either through conditional compilation in- `build.rs`, or through backfills that also work on older versions.
- *Deprecations*are kept in sync with the version of Rust they're added in.
- *Unstable APIs*are currently not supported. Please- [file an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/camino-rs/camino/issues/new)if you need an unstable API.

`camino` is designed to be a core library and has a conservative MSRV policy. MSRV increases will only happen for
a compelling enough reason, and will involve at least a minor version bump.

Optional features may pull in dependencies that require a newer version of Rust.

## License

This project is available under the terms of either the [Apache 2.0 license](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-APACHE) or the [MIT
license](https://docs.rs/LICENSE-MIT).

This project's documentation is adapted from [The Rust Programming Language](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/), which is
available under the terms of either the [Apache 2.0 license](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/master/LICENSE-APACHE)
or the [MIT license](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/master/LICENSE-MIT).

# proptest - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/proptest/^1.0.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#proptest-reference-documentation)Proptest Reference Documentation

This is the reference documentation for the proptest API.

For documentation on how to get started with proptest and general usage
advice, please refer to the [Proptest Book](https://proptest-rs.github.io/proptest/intro.html).

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [arbitrary](https://docs.rs/arbitrary/index.html)
- Defines the `Arbitrary`trait and related free functions and type aliases.
- [array](https://docs.rs/array/index.html)
- Support for strategies producing fixed-length arrays.
- [bits](https://docs.rs/bits/index.html)
- Strategies for working with bit sets.
- [bool](https://docs.rs/bool/index.html)
- Strategies for generating `bool`values.
- [char](https://docs.rs/char/index.html)
- Strategies for generating `char`values.
- [collection](https://docs.rs/collection/index.html)
- Strategies for generating `std::collections`of values.
- [num](https://docs.rs/num/index.html)
- Strategies to generate numeric values (as opposed to integers used as bit fields).
- [option](https://docs.rs/option/index.html)
- Strategies for generating `std::Option`values.
- [path](https://docs.rs/path/index.html)- `std`
- Strategies for generating [`PathBuf`] and related path types.
- [prelude](https://docs.rs/prelude/index.html)
- Re-exports the most commonly-needed APIs of proptest.
- [range_](https://docs.rs/range_subset/index.html)- subset - `std`
- Strategies for generating values by taking samples of index ranges.
- [result](https://docs.rs/result/index.html)
- Strategies for combining delegate strategies into `std::Result`s.
- [sample](https://docs.rs/sample/index.html)
- Strategies for generating values by taking samples of collections.
- [strategy](https://docs.rs/strategy/index.html)
- Defines the core traits used by Proptest.
- [string](https://docs.rs/string/index.html)- `std`
- Strategies for generating strings and byte strings from regular expressions.
- [test_](https://docs.rs/test_runner/index.html)- runner
- State and functions for running proptest tests.
- [tuple](https://docs.rs/tuple/index.html)
- Support for combining strategies into tuples.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_assert.html)- assert
- Similar to `assert!`from std, but returns a test failure instead of panicking if the condition fails.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_assert_eq.html)- assert_ - eq
- Similar to `assert_eq!`from std, but returns a test failure instead of panicking if the condition fails.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_assert_ne.html)- assert_ - ne
- Similar to `assert_ne!`from std, but returns a test failure instead of panicking if the condition fails.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_assume.html)- assume
- Rejects the test input if assumptions are not met.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_compose.html)- compose
- Convenience to define functions which produce new strategies.
- [prop_](https://docs.rs/macro.prop_oneof.html)- oneof
- Produce a strategy which picks one of the listed choices.
- [proptest](https://docs.rs/macro.proptest.html)
- Easily define `proptest`tests.

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [property_](https://docs.rs/attr.property_test.html)- test - `attr-macro`
- The `property_test`procedural macro simplifies the creation of property-based tests using the`proptest`crate. This macro provides a more concise syntax for writing tests that automatically generate test cases based on properties.

# serde_core - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde_core/^1/

## Expand description

Serde is a framework for * ser*ializing and

*serializing Rust data structures efficiently and generically.*

**de**The `serde_core` crate contains Serde’s trait definitions with **no support
for #[derive()]**.

In crates that derive an implementation of `Serialize` or `Deserialize`, you
must depend on the [ serde](https://crates.io/crates/serde) crate, not

`serde_core`.In crates that handwrite implementations of Serde traits, or only use them
as trait bounds, depending on `serde_core` is permitted. But `serde`
re-exports all of these traits and can be used for this use case too. If in
doubt, disregard `serde_core` and always use `serde`.

Crates that depend on `serde_core` instead of `serde` are able to compile in
parallel with `serde_derive` even when `serde`’s “derive” feature is turned on,
as shown in the following build timings.

| When `serde_json`depends on`serde` |

| When `serde_json`depends on`serde_core` |

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [de](https://docs.rs/de/index.html)
- Generic data structure deserialization framework.
- [ser](https://docs.rs/ser/index.html)
- Generic data structure serialization framework.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [forward_](https://docs.rs/macro.forward_to_deserialize_any.html)- to_ - deserialize_ - any
- Helper macro when implementing the `Deserializer`part of a new data format for Serde.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be deserialized from any data format supported by Serde.
- [Deserializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserializer.html)
- A **data format**that can deserialize any data structure supported by Serde.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Serialize.html)
- A **data structure**that can be serialized into any data format supported by Serde.
- [Serializer](https://docs.rs/trait.Serializer.html)
- A **data format**that can serialize any data structure supported by Serde.

# bincode - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/bincode/^1/

## Expand description

Bincode is a crate for encoding and decoding using a tiny binary serialization strategy. Using it, you can easily go from having an object in memory, quickly serialize it to bytes, and then deserialize it back just as fast!

[§](https://docs.rs#using-basic-functions)Using Basic Functions

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
fn main() {
    // The object that we will serialize.
    let target: Option<String>  = Some("hello world".to_string());
    let encoded: Vec<u8> = bincode::serialize(&target).unwrap();
    let decoded: Option<String> = bincode::deserialize(&encoded[..]).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(target, decoded);
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#128bit-numbers)128bit numbers

Support for `i128` and `u128` is automatically enabled on Rust toolchains

# serde - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde/^1.0.223/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#serde)Serde

Serde is a framework for * ser*ializing and

*serializing Rust data structures efficiently and generically.*

**de**The Serde ecosystem consists of data structures that know how to serialize and deserialize themselves along with data formats that know how to serialize and deserialize other things. Serde provides the layer by which these two groups interact with each other, allowing any supported data structure to be serialized and deserialized using any supported data format.

See the Serde website [https://serde.rs](https://serde.rs) for additional documentation and
usage examples.

[§](https://docs.rs#design)Design

Where many other languages rely on runtime reflection for serializing data,
Serde is instead built on Rust’s powerful trait system. A data structure
that knows how to serialize and deserialize itself is one that implements
Serde’s `Serialize` and `Deserialize` traits (or uses Serde’s derive
attribute to automatically generate implementations at compile time). This
avoids any overhead of reflection or runtime type information. In fact in
many situations the interaction between data structure and data format can
be completely optimized away by the Rust compiler, leaving Serde
serialization to perform the same speed as a handwritten serializer for the
specific selection of data structure and data format.

[§](https://docs.rs#data-formats)Data formats

The following is a partial list of data formats that have been implemented for Serde by the community.

- [JSON](https://github.com/serde-rs/json), the ubiquitous JavaScript Object Notation used by many HTTP APIs.
- [Postcard](https://github.com/jamesmunns/postcard), a no_std and embedded-systems friendly compact binary format.
- [CBOR](https://github.com/enarx/ciborium), a Concise Binary Object Representation designed for small message size without the need for version negotiation.
- [YAML](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-yaml), a self-proclaimed human-friendly configuration language that ain’t markup language.
- [MessagePack](https://github.com/3Hren/msgpack-rust), an efficient binary format that resembles a compact JSON.
- [TOML](https://docs.rs/toml), a minimal configuration format used by- [Cargo](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html).
- [Pickle](https://github.com/birkenfeld/serde-pickle), a format common in the Python world.
- [RON](https://github.com/ron-rs/ron), a Rusty Object Notation.
- [BSON](https://github.com/mongodb/bson-rust), the data storage and network transfer format used by MongoDB.
- [Avro](https://docs.rs/apache-avro), a binary format used within Apache Hadoop, with support for schema definition.
- [JSON5](https://github.com/callum-oakley/json5-rs), a superset of JSON including some productions from ES5.
- [URL](https://docs.rs/serde_qs)query strings, in the x-www-form-urlencoded format.
- [Starlark](https://github.com/dtolnay/serde-starlark), the format used for describing build targets by the Bazel and Buck build systems.- *(serialization only)*
- [Envy](https://github.com/softprops/envy), a way to deserialize environment variables into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [Envy Store](https://github.com/softprops/envy-store), a way to deserialize- [AWS Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html)parameters into Rust structs.- *(deserialization only)*
- [S-expressions](https://github.com/rotty/lexpr-rs), the textual representation of code and data used by the Lisp language family.
- [D-Bus](https://docs.rs/zvariant)’s binary wire format.
- [FlexBuffers](https://github.com/google/flatbuffers/tree/master/rust/flexbuffers), the schemaless cousin of Google’s FlatBuffers zero-copy serialization format.
- [Bencode](https://github.com/P3KI/bendy), a simple binary format used in the BitTorrent protocol.
- [Token streams](https://github.com/oxidecomputer/serde_tokenstream), for processing Rust procedural macro input.- *(deserialization only)*
- [DynamoDB Items](https://docs.rs/serde_dynamo), the format used by- [rusoto_dynamodb](https://docs.rs/rusoto_dynamodb)to transfer data to and from DynamoDB.
- [Hjson](https://github.com/Canop/deser-hjson), a syntax extension to JSON designed around human reading and editing.- *(deserialization only)*
- [CSV](https://docs.rs/csv), Comma-separated values is a tabular text file format.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

# serde_bytes - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/serde_bytes/^0.11.8/

## Expand description

Wrapper types to enable optimized handling of `&[u8]` and `Vec<u8>`.

Without specialization, Rust forces Serde to treat `&[u8]` just like any
other slice and `Vec<u8>` just like any other vector. In reality this
particular slice and vector can often be serialized and deserialized in a
more efficient, compact representation in many formats.

When working with such a format, you can opt into specialized handling of
`&[u8]` by wrapping it in `serde_bytes::Bytes` and `Vec<u8>` by wrapping it
in `serde_bytes::ByteBuf`.

Additionally this crate supports the Serde `with` attribute to enable
efficient handling of `&[u8]` and `Vec<u8>` in structs without needing a
wrapper type.

```
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
#[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
struct Efficient<'a> {
    #[serde(with = "serde_bytes")]
    bytes: &'a [u8],
    #[serde(with = "serde_bytes")]
    byte_buf: Vec<u8>,
    #[serde(with = "serde_bytes")]
    byte_array: [u8; 314],
}
```
## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Byte](https://docs.rs/struct.ByteArray.html)- Array
- Wrapper around `[u8; N]`to serialize and deserialize efficiently.
- [ByteBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.ByteBuf.html)
- Wrapper around `Vec<u8>`to serialize and deserialize efficiently.
- [Bytes](https://docs.rs/struct.Bytes.html)
- Wrapper around `[u8]`to serialize and deserialize efficiently.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Deserialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Deserialize.html)
- Types that can be deserialized via `#[serde(with = "serde_bytes")]`.
- [Serialize](https://docs.rs/trait.Serialize.html)
- Types that can be serialized via `#[serde(with = "serde_bytes")]`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [deserialize](https://docs.rs/fn.deserialize.html)
- Serde `deserialize_with`function to deserialize bytes efficiently.
- [serialize](https://docs.rs/fn.serialize.html)
- Serde `serialize_with`function to serialize bytes efficiently.

# camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/camino/1.2.4/target-redirect/camino/

## Expand description

UTF-8 encoded paths.

`camino` is an extension of the [ std::path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/index.html) module that adds new

[and](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html)

`Utf8PathBuf`[types. These are like the standard library’s](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`[and](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html)

`PathBuf`[types, except they are guaranteed to only contain UTF-8 encoded data. Therefore, they expose the ability to get their contents as strings, they implement](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html)

`Path`[, etc.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Display.html)

`Display`The [ std::path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/index.html) types are not guaranteed to be valid UTF-8. This is the right decision for the standard library,
since it must be as general as possible. However, on all platforms, non-Unicode paths are vanishingly uncommon for a
number of reasons:

- Unicode won. There are still some legacy codebases that store paths in encodings like Shift-JIS, but most have been converted to Unicode at this point.
- Unicode is the common subset of supported paths across Windows and Unix platforms. (On Windows, Rust stores paths
as [an extension to UTF-8](https://simonsapin.github.io/wtf-8/), and converts them to UTF-16 at Win32 API boundaries.)
- There are already many systems, such as Cargo, that only support UTF-8 paths. If your own tool interacts with any such system, you can assume that paths are valid UTF-8 without creating any additional burdens on consumers.
- The [“makefile problem”](https://www.mercurial-scm.org/wiki/EncodingStrategy#The_.22makefile_problem.22)(which also applies to`Cargo.toml`, and any other metadata file that lists the names of other files) has*no general, cross-platform solution*in systems that support non-UTF-8 paths. However, restricting paths to UTF-8 eliminates this problem.

Therefore, many programs that want to manipulate paths *do* assume they contain UTF-8 data, and convert them to [ str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)s
as  necessary. However, because this invariant is not encoded in the

[type, conversions such as](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html)

`Path``path.to_str().unwrap()` need to be repeated again and again, creating a frustrating experience.Instead, `camino` allows you to check that your paths are UTF-8 *once*, and then manipulate them
as valid UTF-8 from there on, avoiding repeated lossy and confusing conversions.

# Utf8PathBuf in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.1.4/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html

`pub struct Utf8PathBuf(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

An owned, mutable UTF-8 path (akin to [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)).

This type provides methods like [ push](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html#method.push) and

[that mutate the path in place. It also implements](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html#method.set_extension)

`set_extension`[to](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/deref/trait.Deref.html)

`Deref`[, meaning that all methods on](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`[slices are available on](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`[values as well.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html)

`Utf8PathBuf`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

You can use [ push](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html#method.push) to build up a

[from components:](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html)

`Utf8PathBuf````
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let mut path = Utf8PathBuf::new();
path.push(r"C:\");
path.push("windows");
path.push("system32");
path.set_extension("dll");
```
However, [ push](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html#method.push) is best used for dynamic situations. This is a better way
to do this when you know all of the components ahead of time:

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let path: Utf8PathBuf = [r"C:\", "windows", "system32.dll"].iter().collect();
```
We can still do better than this! Since these are all strings, we can use
[ From::from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html#tymethod.from):

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let path = Utf8PathBuf::from(r"C:\windows\system32.dll");
```
Which method works best depends on what kind of situation you’re in.

Consumes and leaks the [ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html), returning a mutable reference to the contents,

`&'a mut Utf8Path`.The caller has free choice over the returned lifetime, including ’static. Indeed, this function is ideally used for data that lives for the remainder of the program’s life, as dropping the returned reference will cause a memory leak.

It does not reallocate or shrink the [ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html), so the leaked allocation may include
unused capacity that is not part of the returned slice. If you want to discard excess
capacity, call

[, and then](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html#method.into_boxed_path)

`into_boxed_path`[instead. However, keep in mind that trimming the capacity may result in a reallocation and copy.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html#method.leak)

`Box::leak`*Requires Rust 1.89 or newer.*

Extends `self` with `path`.

If `path` is absolute, it replaces the current path.

On Windows:

- if `path`has a root but no prefix (e.g.,`\windows`), it replaces everything except for the prefix (if any) of`self`.
- if `path`has a prefix but no root, it replaces`self`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

Pushing a relative path extends the existing path:

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let mut path = Utf8PathBuf::from("/tmp");
path.push("file.bk");
assert_eq!(path, Utf8PathBuf::from("/tmp/file.bk"));
```
Pushing an absolute path replaces the existing path:

```
use camino::Utf8PathBuf;
let mut path = Utf8PathBuf::from("/tmp");
path.push("/etc");
assert_eq!(path, Utf8PathBuf::from("/etc"));
```
Truncates `self` to [ self.parent](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.parent).

Returns `false` and does nothing if [ self.parent](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.parent) is

[. Otherwise, returns](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None``true`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```

p.pop();
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("/spirited"), p);

```

Returns `true` if the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) is absolute, i.e., if it is independent of
the current directory.

-
On Unix, a path is absolute if it starts with the root, so `is_absolute`and`has_root`
-
On Windows, a path is absolute if it has a prefix and starts with the root: `C:\windows`is absolute, while`C:temp`and`\temp`are not.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-18)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("foo.txt").is_absolute());
```
Returns `true` if the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) has a root.

-
On Unix, a path has a root if it begins with `/`.
-
On Windows, a path has a root if it: - has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g., `\windows`
- has a prefix followed by a separator, e.g., `C:\windows`but not`C:windows`
- has any non-disk prefix, e.g., `\\server\share`

- has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g.,

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-20)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(Utf8Path::new("/etc/passwd").has_root());
```

Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path terminates in a root or prefix.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-21)Examples

The iterator will yield the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) that is returned if the

[method is used zero or more times. That means, the iterator will yield](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.parent)

`parent``&self`, `&self.parent().unwrap()`,
`&self.parent().unwrap().parent().unwrap()` and so on. If the [method returns](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.parent)

`parent`[, the iterator will do likewise. The iterator will always yield at least one value, namely](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

```

assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar")));

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1300-1302)#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1300-1302)

#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Produces an iterator over the [ Utf8Component](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Component.html)s of the path.

When parsing the path, there is a small amount of normalization:

-
Repeated separators are ignored, so `a/b`and`a//b`both have`a`and`b`as components.
-
Occurrences of `.`are normalized away, except if they are at the beginning of the path. For example,`a/./b`,`a/b/`,`a/b/.`and`a/b`all have`a`and`b`as components, but`./a/b`starts with an additional`CurDir`
-
A trailing slash is normalized away, `/a/b`and`/a/b/`are equivalent.

Note that no other normalization takes place; in particular, `a/c`
and `a/b/../c` are distinct, to account for the possibility that `b`
is a symbolic link (so its parent isn’t `a`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-35)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path};
let mut components = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").components();
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::RootDir));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("tmp")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("foo.txt")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), None)
```
Produces an iterator over the path’s components viewed as [ str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)
slices.

For more information about the particulars of how the path is separated
into components, see [ components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.components).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-36)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let mut it = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").iter();
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some(std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR.to_string().as_str()));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("tmp"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("foo.txt"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), None)
```

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the destination file.

This is an alias to [ fs::metadata](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.metadata.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-37)Examples

```

let path = Utf8Path::new("/Minas/tirith");

println!("{:?}", metadata.file_type());
```

Returns `true` if the path points at an existing entity.

Warning: this method may be error-prone, consider using [ try_exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.try_exists) instead!
It also has a risk of introducing time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
permission error, this will return `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-45)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt").exists());
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1581-1587)#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1581-1587)

#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)>

Returns `Ok(true)` if the path points at an existing entity.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `Ok(false)`.

As opposed to the [ exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.exists) method, this one doesn’t silently ignore errors
unrelated to the path not existing. (E.g. it will return

[in case of permission denied on some of the parent directories.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)

`Err`Note that while this avoids some pitfalls of the `exists()` method, it still can not
prevent time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs. You should only use it in scenarios
where those bugs are not an issue.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-46)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(
    !Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt")
        .try_exists()
        .expect("Can't check existence of file does_not_exist.txt")
);
assert!(Utf8Path::new("/root/secret_file.txt").try_exists().is_err());
```

### impl [Arbitrary](https://docs.rs/proptest/1.11.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proptest/arbitrary/traits/trait.Arbitrary.html) for [Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html)

**crate feature**only.

`proptest1`The [ Arbitrary](https://docs.rs/proptest/1.11.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proptest/arbitrary/traits/trait.Arbitrary.html) impl for

`Utf8PathBuf` returns a path with between 0 and 8 components,
joined by the [for the platform. (Each component is randomly generated, and may itself contain one or more separators.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/constant.MAIN_SEPARATOR.html)

`MAIN_SEPARATOR`On Unix, this generates an absolute path half of the time and a relative path the other half.

On Windows, this implementation doesn’t currently generate
[ Utf8PrefixComponent](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html) instances, though in the future it might.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#602-606)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-DerefMut-for-Utf8PathBuf)### impl [DerefMut](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/deref/trait.DerefMut.html) for [Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html)

Available on `path_buf_deref_mut`*Requires Rust 1.68 or newer.*

# Utf8Path in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.1.4/struct.Utf8Path.html

`pub struct Utf8Path(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

A slice of a UTF-8 path (akin to [ str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)).

This type supports a number of operations for inspecting a path, including
breaking the path into its components (separated by `/` on Unix and by either
`/` or `\` on Windows), extracting the file name, determining whether the path
is absolute, and so on.

This is an *unsized* type, meaning that it must always be used behind a
pointer like `&` or [ Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html). For an owned version of this type,
see

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html)

`Utf8PathBuf`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
// Note: this example does work on Windows
let path = Utf8Path::new("./foo/bar.txt");
let parent = path.parent();
assert_eq!(parent, Some(Utf8Path::new("./foo")));
let file_stem = path.file_stem();
assert_eq!(file_stem, Some("bar"));
let extension = path.extension();
assert_eq!(extension, Some("txt"));
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Directly wraps a string slice as a [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) slice.

This is a cost-free conversion.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
Utf8Path::new("foo.txt");
```
You can create [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)s from

[s, or even other](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

`String`[s:](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path````

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#854-856)#### pub fn [is_absolute](https://docs.rs#method.is_absolute)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#854-856)

#### pub fn [is_absolute](https://docs.rs#method.is_absolute)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Returns `true` if the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) is absolute, i.e., if it is independent of
the current directory.

-
On Unix, a path is absolute if it starts with the root, so `is_absolute`and`has_root`
-
On Windows, a path is absolute if it has a prefix and starts with the root: `C:\windows`is absolute, while`C:temp`and`\temp`are not.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("foo.txt").is_absolute());
```
Returns `true` if the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) has a root.

-
On Unix, a path has a root if it begins with `/`.
-
On Windows, a path has a root if it: - has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g., `\windows`
- has a prefix followed by a separator, e.g., `C:\windows`but not`C:windows`
- has any non-disk prefix, e.g., `\\server\share`

- has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g.,

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-10)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(Utf8Path::new("/etc/passwd").has_root());
```
Returns the [ Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html) without its final component, if there is one.

Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path terminates in a root or prefix.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-11)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let path = Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar");
let parent = path.parent().unwrap();
assert_eq!(parent, Utf8Path::new("/foo"));
let grand_parent = parent.parent().unwrap();
assert_eq!(grand_parent, Utf8Path::new("/"));
assert_eq!(grand_parent.parent(), None);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#954-956)#### pub fn [ancestors](https://docs.rs#method.ancestors)(&self) -> [Utf8Ancestors](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Ancestors.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#954-956)

#### pub fn [ancestors](https://docs.rs#method.ancestors)(&self) -> [Utf8Ancestors](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Ancestors.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Produces an iterator over [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) and its ancestors.

The iterator will yield the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) that is returned if the

[method is used zero or more times. That means, the iterator will yield](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.parent)

`parent``&self`, `&self.parent().unwrap()`,
`&self.parent().unwrap().parent().unwrap()` and so on. If the [method returns](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.parent)

`parent`[, the iterator will do likewise. The iterator will always yield at least one value, namely](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None``&self`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-12)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let mut ancestors = Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar").ancestors();
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/foo")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), None);
let mut ancestors = Utf8Path::new("../foo/bar").ancestors();
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("../foo/bar")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("../foo")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("..")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), None);
```
Returns the final component of the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html), if there is one.

If the path is a normal file, this is the file name. If it’s the path of a directory, this is the directory name.

Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path terminates in

`..`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-13)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert_eq!(Some("bin"), Utf8Path::new("/usr/bin/").file_name());
assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("tmp/foo.txt").file_name());
assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/.").file_name());
assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/.//").file_name());
assert_eq!(None, Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/..").file_name());
assert_eq!(None, Utf8Path::new("/").file_name());
```

#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Produces an iterator over the [ Utf8Component](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Component.html)s of the path.

When parsing the path, there is a small amount of normalization:

-
Repeated separators are ignored, so `a/b`and`a//b`both have`a`and`b`as components.
-
Occurrences of `.`are normalized away, except if they are at the beginning of the path. For example,`a/./b`,`a/b/`,`a/b/.`and`a/b`all have`a`and`b`as components, but`./a/b`starts with an additional`CurDir`
-
A trailing slash is normalized away, `/a/b`and`/a/b/`are equivalent.

Note that no other normalization takes place; in particular, `a/c`
and `a/b/../c` are distinct, to account for the possibility that `b`
is a symbolic link (so its parent isn’t `a`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-25)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path};
let mut components = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").components();
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::RootDir));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("tmp")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("foo.txt")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), None)
```
Produces an iterator over the path’s components viewed as [ str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)
slices.

For more information about the particulars of how the path is separated
into components, see [ components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.components).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-26)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let mut it = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").iter();
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some(std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR.to_string().as_str()));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("tmp"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("foo.txt"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), None)
```

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the destination file.

This is an alias to [ fs::metadata](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.metadata.html).

Returns `true` if the path points at an existing entity.

Warning: this method may be error-prone, consider using [ try_exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.try_exists) instead!
It also has a risk of introducing time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
permission error, this will return `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-35)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt").exists());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also)See Also

This is a convenience function that coerces errors to false. If you want to
check errors, call [ fs::metadata](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.metadata.html).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1581-1587)#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1581-1587)

#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)>

Returns `Ok(true)` if the path points at an existing entity.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `Ok(false)`.

As opposed to the [ exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.exists) method, this one doesn’t silently ignore errors
unrelated to the path not existing. (E.g. it will return

[in case of permission denied on some of the parent directories.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)

`Err`Note that while this avoids some pitfalls of the `exists()` method, it still can not
prevent time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs. You should only use it in scenarios
where those bugs are not an issue.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-36)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(
    !Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt")
        .try_exists()
        .expect("Can't check existence of file does_not_exist.txt")
);
assert!(Utf8Path::new("/root/secret_file.txt").try_exists().is_err());
```

`Ok`Converts a [ Box<Utf8Path>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html) into a

[without copying or allocating.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)

`Box<Path>`This is equivalent to the `From<Box<Utf8Path>> for Box<Path>` implementation,
but may aid in type inference.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-40)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Path, Utf8PathBuf};
use std::path::Path;
let utf8_path_buf = Utf8PathBuf::from("foo.txt");
let boxed_utf8_path = utf8_path_buf.into_boxed_path();
let boxed_std_path = boxed_utf8_path.into_std_boxed_path();
assert_eq!(boxed_std_path.to_str(), Some("foo.txt"));
// Convert back to a Box<Utf8Path>.
let new_boxed_utf8_path = Utf8Path::from_boxed_path(boxed_std_path).unwrap();
assert_eq!(&*new_boxed_utf8_path, Utf8Path::new("foo.txt"));
```
Creates a new [ Box<Utf8Path>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html) from a

[containing valid UTF-8 characters, without copying or allocating.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)

`Box<Path>`Errors with the original [ Box<Path>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html) if it is not valid UTF-8.

For a version that returns a type that implements [ std::error::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/error/trait.Error.html),
see

[.](https://docs.rs#impl-TryFrom%3CBox%3CPath%3E%3E-for-Box%3CUtf8Path%3E)

`TryFrom<Box<Path>>`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-41)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::path::Path;
let unicode_path: Box<Path> = Path::new("/valid/unicode").into();
Utf8Path::from_boxed_path(unicode_path).expect("valid Unicode path succeeded");
// Paths on Unix can be non-UTF-8.
let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
let non_unicode_path: Box<Path> = Path::new(non_unicode_str).into();
Utf8Path::from_boxed_path(non_unicode_path).expect_err("non-Unicode path failed");
```

`Box<Utf8Path>` returns a path with between 0 and 8 components,

`MAIN_SEPARATOR`On Unix, this generates an absolute path half of the time and a relative path the other half.

On Windows, this implementation doesn’t currently generate
[ Utf8PrefixComponent](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html) instances, though in the future it might.

# FromBoxedPathError in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.1.4/struct.FromBoxedPathError.html

`pub struct FromBoxedPathError { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A possible error value while converting a [ Box<Path>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html) to a

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)

`Box<Utf8Path>`Produced by the [ TryFrom<Box<Path>>](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#impl-TryFrom%3CBox%3CPath%3E%3E-for-Box%3CUtf8Path%3E) implementation for

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)

`Box<Utf8Path>`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Path, FromBoxedPathError};
use std::convert::{TryFrom, TryInto};
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::path::Path;
let unicode_path: Box<Path> = Path::new("/valid/unicode").into();
let utf8_path: Box<Utf8Path> = unicode_path.try_into().expect("valid Unicode path succeeded");
// Paths on Unix can be non-UTF-8.
let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
let non_unicode_path: Box<Path> = Path::new(non_unicode_str).into();
let err: FromBoxedPathError = <Box<Utf8Path>>::try_from(non_unicode_path.clone())
    .expect_err("non-Unicode path failed");
assert_eq!(err.as_path(), &*non_unicode_path);
assert_eq!(err.into_boxed_path(), non_unicode_path);
```

A possible error value while converting a [ OsString](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/ffi/os_str/struct.OsString.html) to a

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html)

`Utf8PathBuf`Produced by the `TryFrom<OsString>` implementation for [ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8PathBuf, FromOsStringError};
use std::convert::{TryFrom, TryInto};
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::str::FromStr;
use std::ffi::OsString;
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
let unicode_string = OsString::from_str("/valid/unicode").unwrap();
let utf8_path_buf: Utf8PathBuf = unicode_string.try_into()
    .expect("valid Unicode path succeeded");
// Paths on Unix can be non-UTF-8.
let non_unicode_string = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF").to_owned();
let err: FromOsStringError = Utf8PathBuf::try_from(non_unicode_string.clone())
    .expect_err("non-Unicode path failed");
assert_eq!(err.as_os_str(), &non_unicode_string);
assert_eq!(err.into_os_string(), non_unicode_string);
```

# Utf8Component in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.1.4/enum.Utf8Component.html

```
pub enum Utf8Component<'a> {
    Prefix(
```
[Utf8PrefixComponent](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html)<'a>),
    RootDir,
    CurDir,
    ParentDir,
    Normal(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)),
}## Expand description

A single component of a path.

A [ Utf8Component](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Component.html) roughly corresponds to a substring between path separators
(

`/` or `\`).This `enum` is created by iterating over [ Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Components.html), which in turn is
created by the

[method on](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.components)

`components`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path};
let path = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo/bar.txt");
let components = path.components().collect::<Vec<_>>();
assert_eq!(&components, &[
    Utf8Component::RootDir,
    Utf8Component::Normal("tmp"),
    Utf8Component::Normal("foo"),
    Utf8Component::Normal("bar.txt"),
]);
```
## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Prefix)

### Prefix([Utf8PrefixComponent](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html)<'a>)

A Windows path prefix, e.g., `C:` or `\\server\share`.

There is a large variety of prefix types, see [ Utf8Prefix](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Prefix.html)’s documentation
for more.

Does not occur on Unix.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RootDir)

### RootDir

The root directory component, appears after any prefix and before anything else.

It represents a separator that designates that a path starts from root.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CurDir)

### CurDir

A reference to the current directory, i.e., `.`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ParentDir)

### ParentDir

A reference to the parent directory, i.e., `..`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Normal)

### Normal(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html))

A normal component, e.g., `a` and `b` in `a/b`.

This variant is the most common one, it represents references to files or directories.

An iterator over the [ Utf8Component](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Component.html)s of a

[. See its documentation for more.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let path = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo/bar.txt");

}
```

# Utf8DirEntry in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.1.4/struct.Utf8DirEntry.html

`pub struct Utf8DirEntry { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Entries returned by the [ ReadDirUtf8](https://docs.rs/struct.ReadDirUtf8.html) iterator.

An instance of [ Utf8DirEntry](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8DirEntry.html) represents an entry inside of a directory on the filesystem. Each
entry can be inspected via methods to learn about the full path or possibly other metadata.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#2424-2575)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Utf8DirEntry)### impl [Utf8DirEntry](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8DirEntry.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#2424-2575)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Utf8DirEntry)

### impl [Utf8DirEntry](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8DirEntry.html)

Returns the full path to the file that this entry represents.

The full path is created by joining the original path to `read_dir`
with the filename of this entry.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    for entry in Utf8Path::new(".").read_dir_utf8()? {
        let dir = entry?;
        println!("{}", dir.path());
    }
    Ok(())
}
```
This prints output like:

```
./whatever.txt
./foo.html
./hello_world.rs
```
The exact text, of course, depends on what files you have in `.`.

Returns the metadata for the file that this entry points at.

This function will not traverse symlinks if this entry points at a symlink. To traverse
symlinks use [ Utf8Path::metadata](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.metadata) or

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/struct.File.html#method.metadata)

`fs::File::metadata`[§](https://docs.rs#platform-specific-behavior)Platform-specific behavior

On Windows this function is cheap to call (no extra system calls
needed), but on Unix platforms this function is the equivalent of
calling `symlink_metadata` on the path.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
if let Ok(entries) = Utf8Path::new(".").read_dir_utf8() {
    for entry in entries {
        if let Ok(entry) = entry {
            // Here, `entry` is a `Utf8DirEntry`.
            if let Ok(metadata) = entry.metadata() {
                // Now let's show our entry's permissions!
                println!("{}: {:?}", entry.path(), metadata.permissions());
            } else {
                println!("Couldn't get metadata for {}", entry.path());
            }
        }
    }
}
```
Returns the file type for the file that this entry points at.

This function will not traverse symlinks if this entry points at a symlink.

[§](https://docs.rs#platform-specific-behavior-1)Platform-specific behavior

On Windows and most Unix platforms this function is free (no extra
system calls needed), but some Unix platforms may require the equivalent
call to `symlink_metadata` to learn about the target file type.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
if let Ok(entries) = Utf8Path::new(".").read_dir_utf8() {
    for entry in entries {
        if let Ok(entry) = entry {
            // Here, `entry` is a `DirEntry`.
            if let Ok(file_type) = entry.file_type() {
                // Now let's show our entry's file type!
                println!("{}: {:?}", entry.path(), file_type);
            } else {
                println!("Couldn't get file type for {}", entry.path());
            }
        }
    }
}
```
Returns the bare file name of this directory entry without any other leading path component.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
if let Ok(entries) = Utf8Path::new(".").read_dir_utf8() {
    for entry in entries {
        if let Ok(entry) = entry {
            // Here, `entry` is a `DirEntry`.
            println!("{}", entry.file_name());
        }
    }
}
```

# Utf8PrefixComponent in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.1.4/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html

`pub struct Utf8PrefixComponent<'a>(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

A structure wrapping a Windows path prefix as well as its unparsed string representation.

In addition to the parsed [ Utf8Prefix](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Prefix.html) information returned by

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html#method.kind)

`kind`[also holds the raw and unparsed](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html)

`Utf8PrefixComponent`[slice, returned by](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)

`str`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html#method.as_str)

`as_str`Instances of this `struct` can be obtained by matching against the
[ Prefix variant](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Component.html#variant.Prefix) on

[.](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Component.html)

`Utf8Component`Does not occur on Unix.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path, Utf8Prefix};
use std::ffi::OsStr;
let path = Utf8Path::new(r"C:\you\later\");
match path.components().next().unwrap() {
    Utf8Component::Prefix(prefix_component) => {
        assert_eq!(Utf8Prefix::Disk(b'C'), prefix_component.kind());
        assert_eq!("C:", prefix_component.as_str());
    }
    _ => unreachable!(),
}
```

# Utf8Prefix in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.1.4/enum.Utf8Prefix.html

```
pub enum Utf8Prefix<'a> {
    Verbatim(&'a
```
[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)),
    VerbatimUNC(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), &'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)),
    VerbatimDisk([u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)),
    DeviceNS(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)),
    UNC(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), &'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)),
    Disk([u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)),
}## Expand description

Windows path prefixes, e.g., `C:` or `\\server\share`.

Windows uses a variety of path prefix styles, including references to drive
volumes (like `C:`), network shared folders (like `\\server\share`), and
others. In addition, some path prefixes are “verbatim” (i.e., prefixed with
`\\?\`), in which case `/` is *not* treated as a separator and essentially
no normalization is performed.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path, Utf8Prefix};
use camino::Utf8Prefix::*;
fn get_path_prefix(s: &str) -> Utf8Prefix {
    let path = Utf8Path::new(s);
    match path.components().next().unwrap() {
        Utf8Component::Prefix(prefix_component) => prefix_component.kind(),
        _ => panic!(),
    }
}
assert_eq!(Verbatim("pictures"), get_path_prefix(r"\\?\pictures\kittens"));
assert_eq!(VerbatimUNC("server", "share"), get_path_prefix(r"\\?\UNC\server\share"));
assert_eq!(VerbatimDisk(b'C'), get_path_prefix(r"\\?\C:\"));
assert_eq!(DeviceNS("BrainInterface"), get_path_prefix(r"\\.\BrainInterface"));
assert_eq!(UNC("server", "share"), get_path_prefix(r"\\server\share"));
assert_eq!(Disk(b'C'), get_path_prefix(r"C:\Users\Rust\Pictures\Ferris"));
```
## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Verbatim)

### Verbatim(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html))

Verbatim prefix, e.g., `\\?\cat_pics`.

Verbatim prefixes consist of `\\?\` immediately followed by the given
component.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.VerbatimUNC)

Verbatim prefix using Windows’ * Uniform Naming Convention*,
e.g.,

`\\?\UNC\server\share`.Verbatim UNC prefixes consist of `\\?\UNC\` immediately followed by the
server’s hostname and a share name.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.VerbatimDisk)

### VerbatimDisk([u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html))

Verbatim disk prefix, e.g., `\\?\C:`.

Verbatim disk prefixes consist of `\\?\` immediately followed by the
drive letter and `:`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.DeviceNS)

### DeviceNS(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html))

Device namespace prefix, e.g., `\\.\COM42`.

Device namespace prefixes consist of `\\.\` immediately followed by the
device name.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UNC)

Prefix using Windows’ * Uniform Naming Convention*, e.g.

`\\server\share`.UNC prefixes consist of the server’s hostname and a share name.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Disk)

### Disk([u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html))

Prefix `C:` for the given disk drive.

# absolute_utf8 in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.1.4/fn.absolute_utf8.html

`pub fn absolute_utf8<P: `[AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html)>>(path: P) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<[Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html)>**only.**

`absolute_path`## Expand description

Makes the path absolute without accessing the filesystem, converting it to a [ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html).

If the path is relative, the current directory is used as the base directory. All intermediate
components will be resolved according to platform-specific rules, but unlike
[ canonicalize](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.canonicalize) or

[, this does not resolve symlinks and may succeed even if the path does not exist.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.canonicalize_utf8)

`canonicalize_utf8`*Requires Rust 1.79 or newer.*

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Errors if:

- The path is empty.
- The [current directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/env/fn.current_dir.html)cannot be determined.
- The path is not valid UTF-8.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#posix-paths)POSIX paths

```
fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    use camino::Utf8Path;
    // Relative to absolute
    let absolute = camino::absolute_utf8("foo/./bar")?;
    assert!(absolute.ends_with("foo/bar"));
    // Absolute to absolute
    let absolute = camino::absolute_utf8("/foo//test/.././bar.rs")?;
    assert_eq!(absolute, Utf8Path::new("/foo/test/../bar.rs"));
    Ok(())
}
```
The path is resolved using [POSIX semantics](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/V1_chap04.html#tag_04_13) except that it stops short of
resolving symlinks. This means it will keep `..` components and trailing slashes.

[§](https://docs.rs#windows-paths)Windows paths

```
fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    use camino::Utf8Path;
    // Relative to absolute
    let absolute = camino::absolute_utf8("foo/./bar")?;
    assert!(absolute.ends_with(r"foo\bar"));
    // Absolute to absolute
    let absolute = camino::absolute_utf8(r"C:\foo//test\..\./bar.rs")?;
    assert_eq!(absolute, Utf8Path::new(r"C:\foo\bar.rs"));
    Ok(())
}
```
For verbatim paths this will simply return the path as given. For other paths this is currently
equivalent to calling [ GetFullPathNameW](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-getfullpathnamew).

Note that this [may change in the future](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/index.html#platform-specific-behavior).

# tempfile 3.27.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/tempfile/3.27.0

# tempfile

A secure, cross-platform, temporary file library for Rust. In addition to creating temporary files, this library also allows users to securely open multiple independent references to the same temporary file (useful for consumer/producer patterns and surprisingly difficult to implement securely).

## Usage

Minimum required Rust version: 1.63.0

Add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[]
 = "3"
```
## Supported Platforms

This crate supports all major operating systems:

- Linux
- Android
- MacOS
- Windows
- FreeBSD (likely other BSDs but we don't have CI for them)
- RedoxOS
- Wasm (build and link only, Wasm doesn't have a filesystem)
- WASI P1 & P2.

However:

- Android, RedoxOS, Wasm, and WASI targets all require the latest stable rust compiler.
- WASI P1/P2 does not define a default temporary directory. You'll need to explicitly call `tempfile::env::override_temp_dir`with a valid directory or temporary file creation will panic on this platform.
- WASI P1/P2 does not have file permissions.
- You *may*need to override the temporary directory in Android as well to point at your application's per-app cache directory.

## Example

```
use File;
use ;
```

# fastrand - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fastrand/^2.1.1/

## Expand description

A simple and fast random number generator.

The implementation uses [Wyrand](https://github.com/wangyi-fudan/wyhash), a simple and fast
generator but **not** cryptographically secure.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

Flip a coin:

```
if fastrand::bool() {
    println!("heads");
} else {
    println!("tails");
}
```
Generate a random `i32`:

`let num = fastrand::i32(..);`Choose a random element in an array:

```
let v = vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
let i = fastrand::usize(..v.len());
let elem = v[i];
```
Sample values from an array with `O(n)` complexity (`n` is the length of array):

```
fastrand::choose_multiple([1, 4, 5], 2);
fastrand::choose_multiple(0..20, 12);
```
Shuffle an array:

```
let mut v = vec![1, 2, 3, 4, 5];
fastrand::shuffle(&mut v);
```
Generate a random [ Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html) or

[:](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

`String````
use std::iter::repeat_with;
let v: Vec<i32> = repeat_with(|| fastrand::i32(..)).take(10).collect();
let s: String = repeat_with(fastrand::alphanumeric).take(10).collect();
```
To get reproducible results on every run, initialize the generator with a seed:

```
// Pick an arbitrary number as seed.
fastrand::seed(7);
// Now this prints the same number on every run:
println!("{}", fastrand::u32(..));
```
To be more efficient, create a new [ Rng](https://docs.rs/struct.Rng.html) instance instead of using the thread-local
generator:

```
use std::iter::repeat_with;
let mut rng = fastrand::Rng::new();
let mut bytes: Vec<u8> = repeat_with(|| rng.u8(..)).take(10_000).collect();
```
This crate aims to expose a core set of useful randomness primitives. For more niche algorithms,
consider using the [ fastrand-contrib](https://crates.io/crates/fastrand-contrib) crate alongside this one.

[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- `std`(enabled by default): Enables the- `std`library. This is required for the global generator and global entropy. Without this feature,- `Rng`- `with_seed`
- `js`: Assumes that WebAssembly targets are being run in a JavaScript environment. See the- [WebAssembly Notes](https://docs.rs#webassembly-notes)section for more information.

[§](https://docs.rs#webassembly-notes)WebAssembly Notes

For non-WASI WASM targets, there is additional subtlety to consider when utilizing the global RNG.
By default, `std` targets will use entropy sources in the standard library to seed the global RNG.
However, these sources are not available by default on WASM targets outside of WASI.

If the `js` feature is enabled, this crate will assume that it is running in a JavaScript
environment. At this point, the [ getrandom](https://crates.io/crates/getrandom) crate will be used in order to access the available
entropy sources and seed the global RNG. If the

`js` feature is not enabled, the global RNG will
use a predefined seed.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Rng](https://docs.rs/struct.Rng.html)
- A random number generator.
